title: Ibrahim bin al-Mahdi and the Merchant's Sister (Español)

full_text:
Prince Ibrahim bin al-Mahdi, the uncle of Caliph Al-Ma'mun, was celebrated not only for his royal lineage, but as the supreme melodist of Baghdad, whose voice upon the lute could make stones weep and bring peace to troubled minds.

One afternoon, visiting an affluent silk merchant who was his close friend, Ibrahim found the house wrapped in profound gloom. Servants walked on tiptoe, the fountains were silent, and the merchant sat in his courtyard with torn robes and downcast eyes.

'What sorrow has fallen upon your house, dear brother?' asked the prince.

The merchant sighed: 'My younger sister, the joy of our household, had a bitter quarrel with her betrothed over an idle misunderstanding. Words of pride were spoken, and in anger, they broke their engagement. For seven days she has sat in her room weeping, refusing food, while her betrothed wanders the streets in misery. No words of reason can bridge their pride.'

Ibrahim smiled gently: 'Where words of reason fail, music builds a bridge.'

The prince tuned his lute of cedarwood, sat beside the courtyard fountain, and began to play. His fingers moved across the silk strings like the whispering of spring rain. He sang verses describing the fragile dawn of love, how a stray wind can disturb the blossom, and how the noble heart finds its greatest triumph in stretching forth the hand of forgiveness.

His voice rose with such sublime sweetness, soulful purity, and heartfelt tenderness that the birds in the pomegranate trees fell silent to listen.

From the high latticed window above, a soft weeping was heard. The maiden opened her shutter, dropped an embroidered scarf of forgiveness into the courtyard, and sent her maid to summon her betrothed.

Before the stars appeared, the lovers met beside the fountain, embraced with tears of joy, and set aside their pride forever. The merchant embraced the prince, declaring that his music had saved an entire family from lifelong sorrow.
moral: Art and music have the divine power to heal domestic discord and soften wounded hearts. [ES]
